title: Cyclized Hexapeptide-9 (CHP-9): Anti-Aging Skin Peptide Outperforms Retinol — Research Dossier
excerpt: Cyclized Hexapeptide-9 (CHP-9) is a topical cosmetic peptide that outperformed retinol in a 2025 randomized double-blind clinical trial for reducing wrinkles, improving skin elasticity, pigmentation and barrier repair. First peer-reviewed RCT data for this skin anti-aging peptide — commercially available now.
content:
Status Note: Cyclized Hexapeptide-9 (CHP-9) is a cosmetic-grade ingredient, not a pharmaceutical drug. It is not subject to FDA drug approval and is commercially available in over-the-counter skincare products. This dossier covers its scientific evidence base — primarily its 2025 randomized clinical trial — and relevant mechanistic research.

What Is Cyclized Hexapeptide-9?

Cyclized Hexapeptide-9 (CHP-9; INCI name: Hexapeptide-9) is a synthetic cosmetic peptide consisting of six amino acids arranged in a cyclized (ring) conformation. The cyclization distinguishes it from linear hexapeptide sequences: the ring structure confers greater enzymatic stability in the skin, longer residence time in the dermis, and improved receptor-binding geometry compared to a linear analog with the same amino acid sequence.

CHP-9 is designed to target two of the primary molecular drivers of skin aging: loss of collagen and elastin in the dermal matrix, and MMP-mediated extracellular matrix degradation. It achieves this through a receptor-mediated mechanism that does not involve the retinoic acid receptor (RAR) system — which is why it avoids the irritation, peeling, and photosensitivity associated with retinol while working through complementary pathways.

A 2025 clinical trial published in the Journal of Cosmetic Dermatology (Chang et al., 2025, PMC12207714) provided the first peer-reviewed randomized evidence directly comparing CHP-9 to retinol in the same population — and CHP-9 outperformed retinol across the vast majority of measured outcomes.

Mechanism of Action

Three-Pathway Anti-Aging Activity

PathwayMechanismOutcome
Collagen synthesisStimulates Type I and III collagen production in fibroblasts via TGF-β pathway activationImproved skin firmness and wrinkle depth
MMP inhibitionInhibits MMP-1 (collagenase) and MMP-3 (stromelysin) — enzymes that break down collagen and elastin with ageSlows matrix degradation; preserves existing collagen
Epidermal renewalPromotes keratinocyte turnover via surface receptor signaling (non-RAR mechanism)Improved surface texture, pigmentation evening, barrier repair

Why Cyclization Matters

Linear hexapeptides applied to the skin face two challenges: protease degradation before reaching fibroblasts, and lower receptor-binding affinity. CHP-9''s cyclized ring structure addresses both: the cyclic backbone resists skin proteases that cleave N-terminal and C-terminal bonds of linear peptides, and the constrained conformation positions its pharmacophoric residues in the binding geometry that receptor targets prefer — increasing potency per molecule.

Key Research Findings

Phase 3 Cosmetic RCT — Journal of Cosmetic Dermatology, 2025

Citation: Chang et al., "Novel Cyclized Hexapeptide-9 Outperforms Retinol Against Skin Aging: A Randomized, Double-Blinded, Active- and Vehicle-Controlled Clinical Trial." Journal of Cosmetic Dermatology, 2025. PMC12207714 / PubMed 40586182 / DOI: 10.1111/jocd.70290.

Design: Randomized, double-blinded, three-arm, vehicle- and active-controlled trial. Healthy adult volunteers with aging skin applied one of three serums twice daily for 56 days:

  • 0.002% CHP-9 serum
  • 0.002% retinol serum (active control)
  • Vehicle serum (negative control)

Outcomes measured: Crow''s feet wrinkle count, wrinkle area, and wrinkle roughness; forehead wrinkle number and area; periorbital elasticity; nasolabial elasticity; UV spot pigmentation area; transepidermal water loss (TEWL, a barrier function measure).

Results Summary

OutcomeCHP-9 vs. Retinol
Forehead wrinkle countCHP-9 superior
Forehead wrinkle areaCHP-9 superior
Crow''s feet wrinkle countCHP-9 superior
Crow''s feet wrinkle areaCHP-9 superior
Crow''s feet roughnessEquivalent (not significantly different)
Periorbital skin elasticityCHP-9 superior
Nasolabial skin elasticityCHP-9 superior
Skin pigmentation (UV spots)CHP-9 superior
Barrier function (TEWL)CHP-9 superior

Time course: CHP-9''s relative advantage over retinol grew between Day 28 and Day 56, suggesting time-dependent potency augmentation — the longer-used, the more effective relative to retinol.

Dosing and Application

The following reflects the protocol used in the clinical trial and general cosmetic use guidance — not pharmaceutical prescription information.

  • Concentration used in trial: 0.002% CHP-9 in serum formulation
  • Application frequency: Twice daily (morning and evening) in the trial
  • Formulation: Aqueous serum; applied topically to face
  • Study duration: 56 days; benefit increasing through Day 56 with no plateau
  • Tolerance: No significant irritation reported; compatible with twice-daily use (advantage over retinol, which typically requires tolerance-building and once-nightly application)
  • INCI name for product selection: Look for "Hexapeptide-9" in the ingredient list

Frequently Asked Questions

How does cyclized hexapeptide-9 compare to retinol for reducing wrinkles?

A 56-day randomized double-blind trial (Chang et al., 2025, PMC12207714) directly compared 0.002% CHP-9 and 0.002% retinol applied twice daily. CHP-9 outperformed retinol on all measured endpoints except crow''s feet roughness (equivalent): forehead and crow''s feet wrinkle count, wrinkle area and roughness, skin elasticity at orbital and nasolabial areas, UV spot pigmentation, and barrier function (TEWL). The advantage grew over time — CHP-9''s relative superiority was larger at Day 56 than at Day 28. CHP-9 also lacks retinol''s associated irritation, peeling, and photosensitivity, enabling twice-daily use.

What is the mechanism of action of cyclized hexapeptide-9 for skin anti-aging?

CHP-9 works through three interlocking mechanisms: (1) stimulates Type I and III collagen synthesis in fibroblasts via TGF-β pathway activation; (2) inhibits MMP-1 (collagenase) and MMP-3 (stromelysin), enzymes that break down collagen and elastin with age; (3) promotes epidermal keratinocyte renewal through a non-retinoic acid receptor mechanism. Unlike retinol, which acts through nuclear RAR receptors and carries systemic-like irritation potential topically, CHP-9''s receptor-mediated surface action minimizes irritation risk while achieving comparable or superior activity at the same 0.002% concentration.

Can I use cyclized hexapeptide-9 products now — or is it investigational?

CHP-9 is a cosmetic-grade ingredient — not a pharmaceutical drug — and is already commercially available in over-the-counter skincare products. Unlike the investigational pharmaceutical peptides on this site that require clinical trial participation for access, CHP-9 can be purchased today. When selecting a product, look for "Hexapeptide-9" in the INCI ingredient list. The published trial used 0.002%; most commercial serums target a similar concentration. Evidence is based on a single industry-affiliated RCT; independent replication is ongoing.

Research Limitations and Open Questions

  • Single RCT published (Chang et al., 2025); independent replication not yet available
  • Industry affiliation: authors include Shanghai Kans Biotech affiliation; potential sponsor influence on results
  • Retinol comparator was low-dose (0.002%); no comparison to prescription-strength tretinoin
  • Sample size not fully characterized in available summaries; statistical power details require full paper access
  • No long-term data beyond 56 days; durability of effects not established
  • No data on optimal concentration for commercial products
  • Mechanism studies are largely in vitro; in vivo mechanistic confirmation in human skin biopsies is limited
